hypothesis: Price age and recent peer price changes predict the probability and magnitude of rental-price resets better than unconditional historical increments and the selected residual-widening rule.
design_status: One candidate; no parameter search. All evaluation dates were previously inspected in other project experiments, so this is retrospective evidence, not untouched validation.
targets: Exactly the 37 posted-rental series in data/targets.csv; never join different instruments into one price curve.
secondary_evaluation: All 14 origins, reported separately; never substitutes for the primary promotion gate.
reset_definition: Absolute log change greater than 1e-9. Missing calendar dates are not unchanged observations. Price-age resets to zero after a missing day.
peers: Other target series with the same source_id and instrument_class. Exclude the current series. Use only peer observations dated on or before the feature date; never forward-fill or interpolate.
missing_feature_policy: Missing returns or peer statistics become zero; an actual observed current price and at least 8 own adjacent-day pairs in the preceding 28 days are required, otherwise fall back to Pacific drift.

training.pool: same instrument_class; peer features remain same source plus instrument
training.distance: squared Euclidean distance in fixed scaled features

distribution: Weighted empirical h-day log-return distribution: retains the exact no-change atom and both signs of nonzero returns. Each horizon is learned directly from exact calendar h-day pairs. Combine 80% nearest-neighbor distribution with 20% unconditional same-class distribution using the declared recency weights, then take weighted left-CDF quantiles 0.1,0.5,0.9 and multiply exp(return) by the last observed price. Do not use probability times jump size as a quantile.
fallback: Official Pacific drift at that series/origin/horizon if current feature or training support is insufficient. No widening or post-hoc parameter changes.
ablation: One prespecified no-peer ablation uses the same method with the two peer features removed from distance. Diagnostic only; cannot replace the candidate or be promoted.
comparators: Existing selected calibration-study forecasts on matching dates
scoring: Unmodified Pacific scorer.py for all official scores. Identical valid scored cells across candidate and comparators. Preserve per-cell output.

uncertainty.method: paired bootstrap resampling entire origins, preserving all cells in each sampled origin

promotion_gates_all_required: Positive pooled skill versus both Pacific drift and the selected calibration-study forecast on primary dates
Both paired-bootstrap 95% skill intervals have lower endpoint greater than zero
Mean-series skill versus Pacific is no worse than either comparator and at least zero
Coverage is no farther from 0.80 than the selected comparator
No leakage, invalid quantiles or changed frozen files
middle_prediction_claim: Claim improved middle-price prediction only if official q50 loss is lower than both comparators, with positive lower bootstrap confidence endpoints for the q50-loss improvement; report unchanged/changed median counts regardless.
final_output: Only if all promotion gates pass, save forecasts_price_reset.csv separately; never overwrite forecasts.csv, forecasts_calibrated.csv or forecasts_extended.csv.
falsification: Future-target history perturbation must not alter a forecast at its origin
Zero-change training yields an unchanged-price atom
Signed jump distribution permits increases and decreases
Missing days do not increase observed unchanged-age
No-peer ablation diagnoses whether peer information actually helps
